subject: Short-term tenant audit log retention for post-incident debugging (45-day sampling)
messages:
From: Kira Tanaka <kira.tanaka@auroramed.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: short-term retention of tenant audit logs for incident debugging

Hi Dylan,

We recently had a production issue that affected a small subset of sessions for our tenant. Our SOC/IR team is requesting that Redwood retain full tenant audit logs for those affected sessions for 45 days (instead of the standard 14) to support pending forensic work and SAR responses. The impacted timeframe is 2026-12-10 02:00–06:00 UTC and affects tenant id: aurora-tenant-7.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- create a scoped retention exception for just aurora-tenant-7 and the specific session window
- provide an audit trail proving eventual deletion per our request
- share what compensating controls you can apply while logs are retained (access restrictions, read-only exports, encryption keys duration)

We want the ask to be minimal and timeboxed; we expect to call for deletion after forensic signoff. Please include any additional information you need from us (HIPAA context, PO/contract reference).

Thanks,
Kira
Incident Response Lead
AuroraMed

[attachment: auroramed_sar_scope.docx]

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Kira Tanaka <kira.tanaka@auroramed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2026-12-20 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: short-term retention of tenant audit logs for incident debugging

Kira —

Thanks for the details and the artifact. We can support a scoped, timeboxed retention extension for the specific tenant and time window you listed. High-level plan we propose: 

1) Scope: create a retention carveout that includes only the indexed audit events and session traces for tenant aurora-tenant-7 between 2026-12-10T02:00:00Z and 2026-12-10T06:00:00Z. No other tenants or unrelated telemetry will be affected.

2) Duration: 45 calendar days from the request approval date (we'll start the clock from when we snapshot and export the records for your IR team).

3) Controls while retained:
- Access: retention slice will be stored in a restricted bucket with RBAC permitting only named IR admins (you can provide a small allowlist) and read-only for Redwood support engineers.
- Export/Proof-of-delete: we will provide a signed deletion certificate and a secure hash list of deleted objects once we purge the slice.
- Crypto: objects will be re-encrypted under a short-lived envelope key and keyed rotation will match the 45-day window.

4) Evidence we can ship: retention carveout manifest (internal), export bundle (TLS+GPG wrapped), deletion confirmation (signed log + manifests), and a short runbook describing the purge process.

Next steps: Marissa/Neha — can you confirm the operational cost and whether we need legal sign-off for a customer-managed exception? Kira — if that plan works, can you confirm approval from your security owner and provide the allowlist for who can access the retained slice? We will treat this as a billable ad hoc retention with the deal id HW-INV-3092 per our procurement conversation.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood_log_retention_matrix_v2.pdf]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 2026-12-21 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: short-term retention of tenant audit logs for incident debugging

Looping in procurement/legal baseline: quick internal notes —

- Operational: We can implement a tenant-scoped carveout as an admin operation against the retention index. Estimated run cost: one-time export + storage delta ~ 2.5GB and 45 days of hot storage, ballpark $180.
- Compliance: For HIPAA customers we need an explicit written amendment or PO clause approving the extension. For now mark as "pending customer written approval."
- Evidence package: engineering can produce the deletion certificate + hashes. We should also produce a brief attestation letter describing that the slice was retained only under named RBAC.
- Billing: mark as ad hoc professional services (non-recurring) under HW-INV-3092. Finance will generate an invoice after retention initiation.

Neha — confirm whether we need a SIG/C A I Q addendum for this (I suspect not, but want to be explicit in our response).

—Marissa
Head of Customer Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

Kira —

We have everything we need to proceed pending your written approval. Action items we will take after you reply with authorization: 

- Snapshot and export the specified window; store the export in a restricted bucket; start 45-day retention clock.
- Deliver evidence package within 72 hours of snapshot: retention manifest, export bundle link (sftp), and a signed deletion certificate template.
- Provide an allowlist-based RBAC for access during the 45-day window (please send emails for the three people that should be allowed).

Please reply with a single-line approval in this thread, e.g., "AuroraMed approves retention carveout for aurora-tenant-7 for 45 days and accepts the billing terms (HW-INV-3092)." We'll then create the ticket and share the invoice/confirmation.

Best,
Dylan
